locator.text: Display 155.2, p. 155, in the statement of Lemma 4.4

evidence: paper: X_R = X_i (C P_*)^{10}, \qquad x = X / X_R .

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. First clause identical: `resetRadius Xi C P = Xi * (C * P) ^ 10` is X_R = X_i(CP_*)^{10} term for term (same base X_i, same product C·P_*, same exponent 10); `matchingRadius` instantiates it at `Xi = 110`, the paper's X_i = 110 (p. 150, 'X_i = 110'). Second clause x = X/X_R is not a separate Lean definition: the Lean carries the normalized radius as a multiplicative change of variable, writing the physical radius as `matchingRadius F C * x` throughout NominalProfile.lean (e.g. lines 340, 344, 373, 433), and carries its logarithm as `resetClock C P y = y - 10*log(C*P)`. The rewriting: with y = log(X/X_i), resetClock C P y = log(X/X_i) - log((CP)^{10}) = log(X/(X_i(CP)^{10})) = log(X/X_R) = log x, which is exactly what `matching_clock` proves for X = X_R·x (it returns `Real.log x`). Exponentiating recovers x = X/X_R; positivity of C, P_* and X_i makes the step reversible. `ShapeTransition.resetRadius_mul_separation` (line 351) and `separation T C P = exp T/(C*P)^{10}` (line 326) use the same X_R to encode the companion display x_sep = e^{T_sh}/(CP_*)^{10} (B.38), which corroborates the reading of P as the paper's P_*.
